gemini.rationale: The registrant acquired fee title to real estate and in-place net leases (T4), but the asset management, property management, and leasing processes (T5) and personnel (T6) did not transfer; they were provided by affiliated Cole entities under advisory and property-management agreements. This creates a structural gap between the owned assets (T4) and the unowned processes/people (T5/T6), which was mitigated at closing by the advisory and property management agreements.

grok.rationale: gap_45=1 because the slice states that fee title to the real estate together with the in-place net leases crossed into the registrant while operating tenants and their businesses did not change, and asset-management/property-management processes were not owned by the registrant. gap_56=0 because those same processes and the operating personnel both remained outside the registrant in the sponsor/affiliates and were accessed together under the advisory and property-management agreements; neither tier transferred as owned substrate. gap_mitigated=yes because the slice documents that stack of affiliated advisory and property-management/leasing agreements as the closing-time contractual bridge.

openai.rationale: The slice states that fee title and in-place net leases crossed into the registrant, while operating tenants remained and acquisition, asset-management, and property-management/leasing processes were provided by affiliated entities rather than transferred into the registrant. This documents a product-versus-process ownership mismatch at closing, but the advisory and property-management/leasing agreements contractually bridged that gap. No T5-T6 gap is documented because both the processes and the personnel performing them remained together in the sponsor organization and were supplied under those agreements.
